raw_case_text:
A 50-year-old man working as an employee was admitted to neurosurgery clinic with severe low back, radicular right leg pain and hypoesthesia in right L4-5 dermatomes for 2 months. His past history revealed that he had weight loss, night sweats and chills, fatigue and severe malaise for 4 months, and he consumed unpaesteurized milk and dairy products. On neurological examination there was 3/5 motor strength of right ankle dorsiflexion and hypoesthesia in distribution of right leg L4-5 dermatomes. Brucellosis was common in the area where the patient was living and brucella tube agglutination (Wright) test was routinely studied in suspected patients coming from that area. Brucella tube agglutination (Wright) test was studied in serum sample of the patient and was positive with a titer of 1/640. Brucella melitensis was isolated from blood culture. X-ray of the lumber spine showed massive collapse of L4 vertebral body (Fig. 1A). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed fracture and collapse of the body of L4 vertebrae (Fig. 1B, C). The spinal canal was narroved by posterior elements of the vertebrae, therefore neural tissue was compressed (Fig. 1D).
The patient was taken to the operation emergently a posterior midline approach and bilateral hemilaminotomy were done. Grey-yellow colored pathologic specimen was obtained from vertebral body and epidural space. Neural tissue was decompressed and then posterior L3-5 short segment transpedicular screw fixation and stabilization was performed (Fig. 2). Tricortical iliac crest wedge obtained from the same patient (autograft) was used for fusion. Neurological signs and symtoms of the patient were recovered after the operation. Brucella melitensis was isolated from microbiologic culture of pathologic specimen. Antibiotic therapy was given for brucellar infection as doxycycline 200 mg/day and rifampicin 600 mg/day for 6 months.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 50-year-old male employee presented with a 2-month history of severe low back pain, radicular right leg pain, and right L4-L5 hypoesthesia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced fatigue, severe malaise, night sweats, chills, and weight loss over a 4-month period. For the preceding 2 months, he developed progressively severe low back pain radiating into his right lower extremity accompanied by sensory loss and motor weakness, prompting neurosurgical admission.
subjective.past_medical_history: Occupation: employee residing in an endemic zoonotic region. Epidemiological exposure: consumed unpasteurized milk and dairy products. Prior medical conditions not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Severe low back pain, radicular right leg pain, right leg numbness, fatigue, severe malaise, night sweats, chills, weight loss. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Neurological examination: motor strength of right ankle dorsiflexion reduced to 3/5; hypoesthesia in the distribution of right L4-L5 dermatomes. Vital signs not documented.
objective.routine_investigations: Lumbar spine plain radiography: massive collapse of the L4 vertebral body.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar MRI: fracture and collapse of the L4 vertebral body with spinal canal narrowing caused by posterior vertebral elements and compression of neural tissue. Emergent neurosurgery: posterior midline approach with bilateral hemilaminotomy, debridement of grey-yellow pathologic specimen from vertebral body and epidural space, neural decompression, posterior L3-L5 short-segment transpedicular screw fixation, and autograft fusion using tricortical iliac crest wedge.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Brucellar spondylodiscitis with massive L4 vertebral body collapse, spinal canal stenosis, and neural compression.
Confirmation: Brucella tube agglutination (Wright) test positive at a titer of 1/640; blood culture isolated Brucella melitensis; intraoperative culture of vertebral and epidural pathologic specimens grew Brucella melitensis.
Treatment & Outcome: Emergent surgical decompression and posterior L3-L5 transpedicular screw fixation with autograft fusion; targeted antibiotic therapy administered with oral doxycycline 200 mg/day and rifampicin 600 mg/day for 6 months. Neurological signs, motor strength, and sensory symptoms completely recovered after surgery.
